text:
Olivia Chen: hi team — first day! merged the onboarding kubeconfig with my personal one and now vscode kubectl keeps using my minikube context. How do I make sure I use the company context by default?

Olivia Chen: I did `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config:~/downloads/onboard.yaml kubectl config view --merge --flatten > ~/.kube/merged` then `mv` it into place. But `kubectl current-context` still shows `minikube`.

DevEx Bot: welcome Olivia :wave: Quick checks:
• `kubectl config get-contexts -o name` to see available contexts
• `kubectl config use-context <onboard-context-name>` will switch the active one
• If you want the company context by default, run `kubectl config rename-context onboard@dev onboard-olivia` (unique names help) then `kubectl config use-context onboard-olivia`.

Olivia Chen: `kubectl config get-contexts -o name` shows `minikube`, `onboard-olivia@dev`, `ci-runner@dev`. I tried `use-context onboard-olivia@dev` but vscode still picks minikube.

Raj K.: vscode kubectl extension sometimes reads the file in `~/.kube/config` at startup; make sure you replaced the file (and restarted the extension). Also check if VSCode has a workspace KUBECONFIG env var pointing to your minikube file.

Olivia Chen: restarted and fixed — vscode now shows onboard context. One more thing — I run `kubectl get pods -n onboard-olivia` and get `forbidden`. Who do I ask for namespace access?

DevEx Bot: ping @onboarding-bot here. We normally add new hires to `group:eng-onboarding` which has read access to `onboard-*` namespaces. Post the output of `kubectl config view --minify --raw | grep -E "user:|name:" -A1` (redact tokens) and we'll check group membership.

Olivia Chen: pasted sanitized:```
contexts:
- name: onboard-olivia@dev
  context:
    cluster: dev
    namespace: onboard-olivia
    user: olivia.chen@company
users:
- name: olivia.chen@company (auth-provider: oidc)
```

Onboarding Bot: Thanks Olivia — you are not yet in `eng-onboarding`. I'll create a 48h RoleBinding for `user:olivia.chen@company` -> `Role:onboard-namespace-reader` in `onboard-olivia`. If you need permanent access, reply here and DevEx will open the group-add ticket.

Olivia Chen: rolebinding applied — can list now, thanks! Any tips to avoid this in future?

Raj K.: keep company kubeconfigs separate until you're comfortable merging. Use `--kubeconfig` or set `KUBECONFIG` per shell. When you do merge, `kubectl config view --merge --flatten` then inspect contexts and users before replacing `~/.kube/config`.

Olivia Chen: thanks everyone — super helpful. I'll leave my minikube config separate and rename contexts before merging next time :raised_hands:
